gaps.sentence: The assistant ___ I spoke to was extremely helpful.
gaps.explanation: 'Whom' is the formal object form after a preposition-style clause.

gaps.sentence: That was the year ___ the company nearly went bankrupt.
gaps.hint: time: it happened in that year
gaps.explanation: 'When' is used after 'the year'; 'which' would need 'in which'.

gaps.sentence: We bought a table ___ legs had been damaged in transit.
gaps.hint: possession with a thing: the table's legs
gaps.explanation: 'Whose' can show possession with things too: 'the table whose legs ...' means 'the table's legs'.

gaps.sentence: It is one of the most impressive buildings ___ I have ever seen.
gaps.explanation: After superlative expressions, 'that' is the standard relative pronoun in defining clauses.

gaps.sentence: Everything ___ he said turned out to be true.
The discussion got to a stage ___ nobody was listening any more.
gaps.explanation: 'A stage where ...' means 'a stage at which ...'; the clause has its own subject and verb, so 'which' is impossible.
'Who's' is the contraction of 'who is'; 'whose' shows possession and cannot stand before an adjective alone.

gaps.sentence: The letter ___ arrived this morning is from my aunt.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to the letter, a thing, as the subject of 'arrived'.
